amendment_history.note: الإصدار الأصلي (17 مادة، بلا تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول) -- تصديقاً على نظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية بموجب قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (223) وتاريخ 18/4/1438هـ، بناءً على الأمر الملكي رقم (11332) وتاريخ 6/3/1438هـ.

عدّل المادة (الأولى) (تعريفا "الوزارة" و"الوزير"): إحلال عبارة "الوزارة: وزارة الشؤون البلدية والقروية والإسكان" محل عبارة "الوزارة: وزارة التجارة"، وإحلال عبارة "الوزير: وزير الشؤون البلدية والقروية والإسكان" محل عبارة "الوزير: وزير التجارة"، بحسب نافذة "تعديلات المادة" -- غير منعكس في النص الرئيسي المعروض على صفحة هيئة الخبراء (الذي يُظهر "وزارة التجارة والاستثمار"/"وزير التجارة والاستثمار" منذ 2019 على الأقل)، ولا يطابق تماماً النص الحالي المعروض على الموقع الرسمي للهيئة السعودية للمهندسين ("وزارة البلديات والإسكان"/"وزير البلديات والإسكان") -- انظر known_unresolved_discrepancies، المفتاح engineering_practice_article1_ministry_three_way_discrepancy.

chapter_structure.label_ar: بدون تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول
chapter_structure.title_ar: مواد متسلسلة غير مجمعة تحت أبواب أو فصول رسمية، لا يحمل أي منها عنواناً فرعياً في المصدر: التعريفات (م1) -- اشتراط الاعتماد المهني لمزاولة المهنة (م2) -- حظر مزاولة تخصص أو درجة غير معتمدين (م3) -- حظر تشغيل مهندسين غير معتمدين (م4) -- حظر قبول عمل هندسي إلا من معتمدين (م5) -- شروط الاعتماد المهني (م6) -- إجراءات تقديم طلبات الاعتماد المهني والفصل فيها (م7) -- التزام المعتمد بذكر بياناته على أعماله (م8) -- تحديد الدرجات المهنية ومتطلباتها (م9) -- ترخيص المكاتب والشركات الهندسية (م10) -- عقوبات الغرامة والسجن على مخالفات الاعتماد والترخيص (م11) -- لجان المخالفات الأخرى وعقوباتها (م12) -- جواز النشر على نفقة المخالف (م13) -- ضبط المخالفات (م14) -- إعادة الاعتماد أو الترخيص بعد الشطب أو الإلغاء (م15) -- اللائحة التنفيذية (م16) -- النفاذ (م17).

verification_methodology_note:
Law of the Practice of Engineering Professions «نظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية» -- Royal Decree M/36 dated 19/4/1438هـ (17 Jan 2017G), approved via Council of Ministers Resolution No. 223 dated 18/4/1438هـ (itself based on Royal Order No. 11332 dated 6/3/1438هـ). 17 articles, no أبواب/فصول labels anywhere in the source (a flat sequence).

DISTINCTNESS FROM saudi_engineers_law (decree-number collision re-confirmed independently this pass): this track's own BOE page (lawId ebb751a1-6f0b-4595-9736-a9a700f1f47b) was fetched directly this pass via three independent Wayback Machine snapshots (14 Nov 2019, 27 Nov 2022, 25 Feb 2026) and its own metadata panel reads, verbatim, 'مرسوم ملكي رقم م / 36 بتاريخ 19 / 4 / 1438' -- a decree carrying the SAME bare number (م/36) as, but an entirely different hijri date (19/4/1438هـ, 2017G) from, this corpus's already-ingested saudi_engineers_law track (Royal Decree M/36 dated 26/9/1423هـ, 2002G, 'Law of the Saudi Council of Engineers', a 9-article organizing statute for the Authority itself). This law's own Article 1 DEFINES 'الهيئة' as 'الهيئة السعودية للمهندسين' -- i.e. it presupposes that Authority's prior existence exactly as the saudi_engineers_law track's own official_source.json itself anticipated and flagged (see that track's known_unresolved_discrepancies, key saudi_engineers_companion_practice_law_not_ingested, which named this exact law, decree, date, and lawId in advance). The two laws are genuinely distinct instruments (different subject matter: one organizes the Authority's own governance/membership/finances in 9 articles; this one governs individual/firm licensing, professional accreditation, and disciplinary penalties in 17 articles) that happen to share a decree serial number because Saudi royal-decree numbers are not perpetually unique across all history -- re-confirmed here, independently, as a genuine numbering coincidence and NOT a research error.

PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: laws.boe.gov.sa's live portal was unreachable via direct curl this pass (connection reset, consistent with this corpus's established pattern for this BOE portal). Three independent Wayback Machine snapshots of this exact law's detail URL were fetched via direct curl over the pre-configured proxy (14 Nov 2019, timestamp 20191114042339; 27 Nov 2022, timestamp 20221127194529; 25 Feb 2026, timestamp 20260225165052 -- the most recent of 23 snapshots spanning Nov 2019-Feb 2026 found via the Wayback CDX API) and parsed offline with BeautifulSoup, isolating each article's 'div.HTMLContainer' body text from its 'div.article_btns' amendment-changelog toggle/popup. All 17 'article_item' divs are present, in sequence, in every snapshot. Diffing the three snapshots shows all 17 articles' main-body text is BYTE-IDENTICAL across all three time-points (2019, 2022, 2026); the ONLY difference across the three snapshots is that Article 1 gained a 'changed-article' CSS class and a nested 'تعديلات المادة' changelog popup between the 2019 and 2022 snapshots (consistent with the changelog's own amending-decree date, 7/4/1444هـ, i.e. approx. Oct 2022G) -- strong evidence the other 16 articles are unamended, and that Article 1's changelog was added to BOE's system without any accompanying change to BOE's own main-body text for that article.

SECOND SOURCE: the Saudi Council of Engineers' own official website (saudieng.sa -- this law's own administering regulator, a genuinely separate primary source from BOE, not a re-hosted BOE mirror), which hosts its own PDF copy of this exact law (saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/PracticeSystemNEW.pdf, located via WebSearch and retrieved this pass via a Wayback Machine snapshot dated 15 Jun 2025 after the live saudieng.sa endpoint proved unreachable in this sandbox on direct fetch -- connection reset). Extracted cleanly via pdftotext -layout (no character-scrambling issue of the kind documented elsewhere in this corpus for certain government PDFs). Its cover page independently confirms Royal Decree M/36, 19/4/1438هـ. Its full 17-article body text matches BOE's own 17-article text WORD-FOR-WORD for Articles 2 through 17 inclusive -- a strong, genuinely cross-domain (government legal database vs. the regulating Authority's own site) confirmation of structure, decree identity, and article count. Article 1 is the sole point of divergence between the two sources (see below and known_unresolved_discrepancies).

THIRD-SOURCE STRUCTURAL CROSS-CHECK: a WebSearch aggregation independently corroborates the same decree number (M/36), same hijri date (19/4/1438هـ), and same ratifying Council of Ministers Resolution (223, 18/4/1438هـ), and surfaced this law's own indexing on qanoonsa.com and qanoniah.com under a matching title, further corroborating its continued existence as a distinct, separately-searchable statute. Per this corpus's four-tier verification taxonomy, this qualifies as TIER_1 (BOE, reached via near-live/well-corroborated Wayback snapshots, cross-checked against saudieng.sa's own genuinely separate official PDF for 16 of 17 articles verbatim, further corroborated structurally by qanoonsa.com/qanoniah.com).

ARTICLE 1 -- A GENUINE THREE-WAY DISCREPANCY (handled per this corpus's awqaf_law Article 6 precedent for a changelog 'before'-phrase that does NOT cleanly match the observed main body, rather than the accounting_auditing_law/press_law precedent for a clean substitution): BOE's own changelog popup for Article 1 quotes Council of Ministers Resolution No. (250) dated 7/4/1444هـ as substituting 'الوزارة: وزارة الشؤون البلدية والقروية والإسكان' / 'الوزير: وزير الشؤون البلدية والقروية والإسكان' IN PLACE OF 'الوزارة: وزارة التجارة' / 'الوزير: وزير التجارة'. However, BOE's own main-body text for Article 1 has read 'الوزارة: وزارة التجارة والاستثمار' / 'الوزير: وزير التجارة والاستثمار' (i.e. already includes 'والاستثمار', consistent with the real-world 2019 merger of Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Commerce into the Ministry of Commerce and Investment) at EVERY one of the three independently-checked BOE snapshots, including the earliest (14 Nov 2019) -- meaning the changelog's own quoted 'before' phrase ('وزارة التجارة', without 'والاستثمار') does NOT cleanly match the article's own actual, stable, observed wording at any checked time-point, an internal inconsistency of exactly the kind that blocked mechanical incorporation in this corpus's awqaf_law Article 6 precedent. Compounding this, saudieng.sa's OWN official PDF (Wayback snapshot, 15 Jun 2025 -- more recent than any BOE snapshot checked) shows a THIRD, again-different wording: 'الوزارة: وزارة البلديات والإسكان' / 'الوزير: وزير البلديات والإسكان' (Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing -- the ministry's REAL-WORLD current short name following an administrative renaming/restructuring of the former 'وزارة الشؤون البلدية والقروية والإسكان' some time after Resolution 250's own 1444H/2022G date, not itself logged anywhere in BOE's own changelog for this law). Given three non-reconciling wordings (BOE stale main body; BOE changelog's own instructed substitution, whose 'before' phrase itself does not match BOE's own main body; and saudieng.sa's own current-but-differently-worded text reflecting a subsequent real-world ministry rename), this track does NOT fabricate a merged/reconstructed wording. Following the awqaf_law Article 6 precedent, this track ingests BOE's own consistently-displayed, stable main-body text ('وزارة التجارة والاستثمار'/'وزير التجارة والاستثمار') as Article 1's current 'text', marks legal_status_ar as 'معدلة' (since BOE's own metadata officially flags this article as changed and independent evidence -- Resolution 250 itself, plus saudieng.sa's own divergent-but-clearly-changed wording -- confirms a real supervising-ministry transfer did occur in substance, away from the commerce/investment portfolio toward the municipal/housing portfolio), and documents the full three-way divergence in known_unresolved_discrepancies (key engineering_practice_article1_ministry_three_way_discrepancy) rather than asserting any single wording as definitively current.

STRUCTURE: this Law has NO أبواب/فصول subdivision -- a flat sequence of 17 individually-numbered articles, confirmed by the complete absence of any باب/فصل-prefixed heading anywhere in the archived BOE HTML across all three snapshots, and independently corroborated by the identical flat 17-article sequence on saudieng.sa's own PDF. No article carries an inline topic title in the BOE source (every article heading is a bare ordinal followed only by a colon, e.g. 'المادة الأولى:') -- consistent with this corpus's accounting_auditing_law, nazaha_law, awqaf_law, and saudi_engineers_law precedent for BOE sources lacking inline per-article titles; no title_ar key is used.

REPEAL/PREDECESSOR: no predecessor engineering-practice law or regulation was found to have been repealed or superseded by this Law. A full-text search of this law's own archived HTML for 'يلغى', 'يلغي', 'يحل محل', and related repeal-language turned up zero matches anywhere in the 17 articles or the preamble; Article 17 (the final article) contains only a bare entry-into-force clause ('يعمل بهذا النظام بعد ستين يوماً من تاريخ نشره في الجريدة الرسمية') with no repeal language at all -- unlike e.g. this corpus's press_law (explicit Article 48 repeal of a named 1982 predecessor) or awqaf_law. This is treated as a CONFIRMED NEGATIVE finding (no predecessor instrument exists to ingest, cross-reference, or flag as historical context), not an unresolved research gap -- consistent with this corpus's saudi_engineers_law precedent for the sibling organizing statute, which reached the same negative finding for its own, different, Article 9 general conflict-only repeal clause (this law does not even have that much: it has no repeal clause of any kind, general or specific).

COMPANION INSTRUMENTS IDENTIFIED (NOT INGESTED THIS PASS, per this corpus's one-law-per-pass rule): (1) اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية (this law's own Implementing Regulation, referenced in this law's own Article 16, which requires the Minister to issue it within 90 days of the law's effective date -- located this pass via WebSearch as a standalone PDF hosted at both saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/67.pdf and as a published notice on Umm Al-Qura Gazette's site, uqn.gov.sa/details?p=24294, titled 'اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية'; note this Implementing Regulation has itself been reissued/amended more than once over the years by different supervising ministries per its own successive Umm Al-Qura notices, e.g. a decision by the Ministry of Municipal, Rural Affairs and Housing referenced via qanoonsa.com -- consistent with, and independently corroborating in substance, this law's own Article 1 supervising-ministry transfer discussed above, even though the exact resulting ministry name differs across the sources checked); (2) ميثاق المهندس (the Engineer's Charter, a Board-issued professional-ethics/conduct code referenced within this law's own Article 1 definitions and Article 6(3)'s accreditation requirement to 'pledge to abide by the Engineer's Charter'), most recently reissued per this corpus's saudi_engineers_law track's own prior research (26 Jan 2025 per qanoonsa.com); and (3) لائحة الوظائف الهندسية (the Engineering Positions/Jobs Regulation, a Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development instrument located this pass via WebSearch, hrsd.gov.sa, dated 1446هـ/2024-2025G, and separately referenced in this law's own preamble Council of Ministers Resolution text, clause 'ثانياً', instructing relevant authorities to expedite issuing it). None of these three companion instruments is ingested, fabricated, or partially guessed at in this pass; all are flagged here as candidates for dedicated follow-up ingestion passes (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key engineering_practice_companion_instruments_not_ingested).

No legal text is altered beyond whitespace/typography normalisation needed to render BOE's/saudieng.sa's raw HTML/PDF as plain text (collapsing incidental double-space/tab artifacts from adjacent inline-element rendering into single spaces; and, in Articles 11 and 12 only, removing a purely decorative in-word tatweel/kashida character BOE's own HTML inserts in the word "ريـال" -- normalised to "ريال" -- a stretch-justification typographic artifact carrying no semantic content, consistent with this corpus's established practice of normalising exactly this class of decorative-elongation artifact). Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic text (English descriptions in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en are for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: An earlier pass (documented in this corpus's saudi_engineers_law track's own known_unresolved_discrepancies, key saudi_engineers_companion_practice_law_not_ingested) estimated this law at 17 articles based on a prior fetch of BOE's page (lawId ebb751a1-6f0b-4595-9736-a9a700f1f47b). This pass independently re-verifies that estimate from scratch via three fresh Wayback Machine snapshots (14 Nov 2019, 27 Nov 2022, 25 Feb 2026) and CONFIRMS exactly 17 articles, with no أبواب/فصول subdivision, cross-checked against saudieng.sa's own official PDF copy of the law (16 of 17 articles byte-for-byte/word-for-word identical; Article 1 diverges only in its supervising-ministry naming, see the dedicated discrepancy entry below).

Both this law (Royal Decree م/36, 19/4/1438هـ / 2017G) and this corpus's already-ingested saudi_engineers_law track (Royal Decree م/36, 26/9/1423هـ / 2002G, 'Law of the Saudi Council of Engineers') carry the IDENTICAL bare decree number 'م/36' despite being unrelated instruments roughly 15 hijri years apart, governing entirely different subject matter (this law: individual/firm engineering-practice licensing, professional accreditation, and disciplinary penalties, 17 articles; saudi_engineers_law: the Authority's own governance, membership, and finances, 9 articles). This is an expected artifact of the Saudi royal-decree numbering convention (numbers are not perpetually unique across all administrative periods), independently RE-CONFIRMED this pass via direct examination of this law's own BOE page metadata ('مرسوم ملكي رقم م / 36 بتاريخ 19 / 4 / 1438') and re-confirmed as a genuine two-instrument coincidence, not a research error. This law's own Article 1 defines 'الهيئة' as 'الهيئة السعودية للمهندسين', i.e. it presupposes and references the OTHER track's Authority as an already-existing body rather than repealing or replacing it; the two laws coexist as companion instruments (an organizing/governance statute for the Authority itself, plus a separate practice/licensing/discipline statute for the profession it regulates) -- exactly as the saudi_engineers_law track's own prior research anticipated when it named this law, its decree, its date, and its BOE lawId in advance as the strongest follow-up candidate. Both tracks now cross-reference each other's decree-collision documentation; track_id 'engineering_practice_law' is used throughout this track's own files (distinct from 'saudi_engineers_law') to prevent any registry-level naming collision.

Article 1 (definitions, including 'الوزارة'/'الوزير') carries a single confirmed BOE-logged amendment: Council of Ministers Resolution No. (250) dated 7/4/1444هـ, quoted by BOE's own 'تعديلات المادة' changelog popup as substituting 'الوزارة: وزارة الشؤون البلدية والقروية والإسكان' / 'الوزير: وزير الشؤون البلدية والقروية والإسكان' in place of 'الوزارة: وزارة التجارة' / 'الوزير: وزير التجارة'. However, diffing all THREE independently-fetched BOE Wayback snapshots (14 Nov 2019, 27 Nov 2022, 25 Feb 2026) shows Article 1's own main-body text has read 'الوزارة: وزارة التجارة والاستثمار' / 'الوزير: وزير التجارة والاستثمار' (i.e. ALREADY includes 'والاستثمار', consistent with the real-world 2019 merger of the Ministry of Commerce into the Ministry of Commerce and Investment) at EVERY checked time-point, including the earliest (2019), predating Resolution 250 itself by roughly three years. This means BOE's own changelog 'before' phrase ('وزارة التجارة', without 'والاستثمار') does NOT cleanly match the article's own actual, stable, observed wording at any checked snapshot -- an internal inconsistency of exactly the same class that blocked mechanical changelog incorporation in this corpus's awqaf_law Article 6 precedent (as opposed to this corpus's press_law/accounting_auditing_law precedent, where a clean, matching 'before' phrase permitted safe incorporation of the amended wording). Compounding this, saudieng.sa's own official PDF of this law (Wayback snapshot dated 15 Jun 2025, more recent than any BOE snapshot checked here) shows a THIRD, again-different wording: 'الوزارة: وزارة البلديات والإسكان' / 'الوزير: وزير البلديات والإسكان' (Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing -- this ministry's real-world current short name following an administrative renaming that post-dates Resolution 250's own 1444H/2022G date and is not itself logged anywhere in BOE's own changelog for this law). Given three non-reconciling wordings across two genuinely independent official sources (BOE's own stale main body; BOE's own changelog-instructed substitution, whose quoted 'before' phrase itself does not match BOE's own main body; and saudieng.sa's own current-but-differently-worded text), this track does NOT fabricate, guess, or mechanically merge a resolution. Following the awqaf_law Article 6 precedent, this track ingests BOE's own consistently-displayed, stable main-body wording ('وزارة التجارة والاستثمار'/'وزير التجارة والاستثمار') as Article 1's current 'text' field, while marking legal_status_ar as 'معدلة' (BOE's own metadata officially flags this article as changed, and independent evidence -- Resolution 250 itself, plus saudieng.sa's own divergent wording, plus a qanoonsa.com-indexed Ministry of Municipal, Rural Affairs and Housing decision reissuing this law's own Implementing Regulation -- corroborates that a real supervising-ministry transfer occurred in substance, away from the commerce/investment portfolio and toward the municipal/housing portfolio, even though this track cannot verify a single definitive current wording from its own primary sources). Anyone relying on this track's Article 1 text as definitively identifying the CURRENT named supervising ministry/minister should treat that as unconfirmed by this track's own ingested primary-source text pending a dedicated follow-up verification (e.g. a direct, live fetch of BOE's page, or the Umm Al-Qura Gazette notice for Resolution 250 itself, neither of which was reachable this pass). BOE's own main-body article text for Article 1 is confirmed genuinely stale relative to the current, amended law -- not a proxy or reachability artifact -- since BOE's own metadata flags this article as changed (legal_status معدلة) and multiple independent sources (Council of Ministers Resolution 250 itself, saudieng.sa's own differently-worded current text, and a qanoonsa.com-indexed reissued Implementing Regulation from the Ministry of Municipal, Rural Affairs and Housing) corroborate that a real supervising-ministry transfer occurred, even though the exact current wording could not be confirmed from any single primary source this pass, following the awqaf_law Article 6 precedent for this exact failure mode.

No predecessor engineering-practice/licensing law or regulation was found to have been repealed or superseded by this Law. A full-text search of this law's own archived BOE HTML for repeal-language markers ('يلغى', 'يلغي', 'يحل محل', 'نظام سابق', 'الملغ') returned zero matches anywhere in the preamble or all 17 articles; Article 17 (the law's final article) contains only a bare entry-into-force clause with no repeal language of any kind, general or specific -- unlike e.g. this corpus's press_law (an explicit, specific repeal of a named 1982 predecessor in its own Article 48) or this corpus's saudi_engineers_law (at least a general, conflict-only repeal clause in its own Article 9, naming no specific predecessor). This law has neither. This is treated as a CONFIRMED NEGATIVE finding (no predecessor instrument exists to ingest, cross-reference, or flag as historical context), not an unresolved research gap, consistent with this corpus's saudi_engineers_law precedent for reaching a similar (if not quite as absolute) negative finding for its own, sibling organizing statute.

This law has NO أبواب (parts) or فصول (chapters) -- it is a flat sequence of 17 individually-numbered articles with no grouping/part headers anywhere on BOE's page across any of the three independently-fetched snapshots (no باب/فصل-prefixed heading was found alongside the 17 'article_item' divs in any snapshot), independently corroborated by the identical flat structure on saudieng.sa's own PDF. This track's chapter_structure field reflects this verified flat structure (a single leaf range 1-17) rather than inventing a topical grouping not present in the primary source, consistent with this corpus's saudi_engineers_law and awqaf_law precedent.

This law's BOE-hosted HTML supplies NO inline title text for any of its 17 articles -- every 'h3' heading for an article is a bare ordinal followed only by a colon (e.g. 'المادة الأولى:'), across all three snapshots checked and independently corroborated by the identical heading style on saudieng.sa's own PDF. Consistent with this corpus's accounting_auditing_law, nazaha_law, awqaf_law, and saudi_engineers_law precedent for sources lacking inline per-article titles, no title_ar key is used for any article; section_ar instead carries the constant 'بدون تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول' for structural context, since this law has no أبواب/فصول at all.

Three closely-related companion instruments were identified but are NOT ingested this pass, per this corpus's one-law-per-pass rule: (1) اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية (this law's own Implementing Regulation, required by this law's own Article 16 to be issued by the Minister, in coordination with the Board, within 90 days of the law's effective date; located via WebSearch as a standalone PDF hosted at saudieng.sa/Admin/NPSCERules/67.pdf and as a published notice on Umm Al-Qura Gazette's site, uqn.gov.sa/details?p=24294; this Implementing Regulation has itself apparently been reissued/amended more than once by different supervising ministries per successive Umm Al-Qura notices located via WebSearch, e.g. a decision attributed to the Ministry of Municipal, Rural Affairs and Housing per qanoonsa.com -- circumstantially corroborating, without definitively confirming, this law's own Article 1 supervising-ministry transfer discussed above); (2) ميثاق المهندس (the Engineer's Charter, a Board-issued professional-ethics/conduct code referenced within this law's own Article 1 definitions and Article 6(3)'s accreditation requirement, most recently reissued 26 Jan 2025 per this corpus's saudi_engineers_law track's own prior research via qanoonsa.com); and (3) لائحة الوظائف الهندسية (the Engineering Positions/Jobs Regulation, a Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development instrument located via WebSearch at hrsd.gov.sa, dated 1446هـ, separately referenced in this law's own preamble -- Council of Ministers Resolution 223's own clause 'ثانياً' instructs relevant authorities to expedite issuing it). None of these three companion instruments is ingested, fabricated, or partially guessed at in this pass; all three are flagged here as candidates for dedicated follow-up ingestion passes.
